newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - Oct 29.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - Oct 29.

text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Scottish writer JAMES BOSWELL, who wrote SAMUEL JOHNSON's biography, was born in 1780.
English poet JOHN KEATS was born in London in 1796.

Australian pioneer cyclist SARAH MADDOCK, who was the first woman to cycle from Sydney to Melbourne, was born in 1860. She also did a Melbourne - Brisbane round trip. In a forerunner to cycle shorts she wore black satin underknickerbockers and popularised cycling for Australian women.
French author JEAN GIRADOUX, who wrote "The Madwoman of Chaillot", was born in 1882.
American Broadway star FANNY BRICE, whose life story was immortalised in "Funny Girl", was born in 1891.
German Nazi propaganda chief JOSEPH GOEBBELS, who poisoned himself when the Allies entered Berlin, was born in 1897.
American actor RICHARD DREYFUS, who won an Oscar for his performance in "The Goodbye Girl", was born in 1949. His other starring roles were in "American Graffiti" and "Jaws".

British leadsinger, bassist and songwriter, DAVID PATON, with the band 'Pilot', was born in 1951. Hits included "Magic" (1974) and "January" (1975). As a session musician DAVID recorded with KATE BUSH, CHRIS de BURGH, CHRIS REA and ELTON JOHN.

UK synthesier player, singer and songwriter with 'Blancmange' STEPHEN LUSCOMBE was born in 1954. The group was successful from 1982. Hits included "Living On The Ceiling" (1982), "Blind Vision" (1983) and "Don't Tell Me" (1984).
** EVENTS **
1618 : Sir WALTER RALEIGH, English adventurer who was a
favourite of Queen ELIZABETH I, was executed in London for treason.
1886 : Champion English jockey FRED ARCHER rode his last
race after 16 years and 2746 wins.
1889 : The British South Africa Company, headed by CECIL
RHODES, was granted royal charter by the British government giving it extensive powers and rights in the area which became Rhodesia.
1929 : Prices virtually collapsed at the New York Stock

Exchange on Wall Street. The day became known as "Black Tuesday" and lead to the Great Depression of the 1930s. New York banks attempted to stem the panic on Wall Street. Out-of-town banks withdrew more than two billion dollars from Wall Street, but the local New York banks increased their lending by one billion to prevent a money panic.
1940 : A 31-year-old HAROLD HOLT was recalled from active
service to become minister for Labour and National Service.
1946 : The Sheffield Shield cricket competition resumed

in Brisbane after being abandoned during the war. New South Wales defeated Queensland in the first game and Victoria clinched the first Shield since the war. In 1995 Queensland won the Shield for the first time.
1956 : Israeli forces crossed into the Sinai Peninsula
pushing towards the Suez Canal.
1972 : The Black September guerrilla group hijacked a
Lufthansa Boeing 727 as it flew over Turkey and demanded the release of three colleagues still held for the massacre of Israeli athletes at the Olympic Games.
1978 : MAO TSE TUNG's "Little Red Book" was denounced in

the official Communist Party newspaper. The "Little Red Book" was once the bible of Chinese Communism. It was translated into 80 languages and at one time rivalled the Bible as the world's best seller. The "People's Daily" criticised the book for giving MAO a "God-like status".
1982 : LINDY CHAMBERLAIN was found guilty of murdering

her baby daughter AZARIA. The Darwin court sentenced Mrs CHAMBERLAIN to life imprisonment and her Seventh Day Adventist minister husband MICHAEL was found guilty of being an accessory after the murder. The couple said a dingo had taken their nine-week old baby while they were camping at Ayers Rock. The convictions were later quashed.
1988 : Britain's Olympic middle distance runners
SEBASTIAN COE and STEVE CRAM ran the circuit around Cambridge's Trinity College Great Court. The course must be completed between the first and last clock strokes of 12. COE won.
1995 : 289 people were killed when a crowded underground
train caught fire between stations in Baku, Azerbaijan.
